questions.q: Which organelle is primarily responsible for ATP synthesis and cellular respiration?
questions.exp: Mitochondria generate most of the chemical energy needed to power cellular biochemical reactions.

questions.q: What is the primary end product of glycolysis in animal cells under anaerobic conditions?
questions.exp: In the absence of sufficient oxygen, pyruvate is converted into lactic acid during anaerobic respiration in animals.

questions.q: Which blood component is primarily responsible for oxygen transport throughout the human body?
questions.exp: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which binds oxygen molecules in the lungs and releases them in tissues.

questions.q: Calculate the force required to accelerate a 1200 kg vehicle uniformly at 3 m/s².
questions.exp: Using Newton's Second Law: F = m × a = 1200 × 3 = 3600 N.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2 m/s² for 5 seconds. Calculate the total distance covered.
questions.exp: Using s = ut + ½at²: s = 0 + ½(2)(5²) = 25 m.

What mass of CaCO₃ is required to produce 4.4 g of CO₂ upon complete thermal decomposition? (Ca=40, C=12, O=16)
questions.exp: CaCO₃ -> CaO + CO₂. Molar mass CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol, CO₂ = 44 g/mol. Moles CO₂ = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol. Mass CaCO₃ = 0.1 × 100 = 10.0 g.

questions.q: Calculate the molarity of a solution formed by dissolving 5.85 g of NaCl in distilled water to make 250 cm³ of solution. (Na=23, Cl=35.5)
questions.exp: Molar mass NaCl = 58.5 g/mol. Moles = 5.85 / 58.5 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 0.25 L. Molarity = 0.1 / 0.25 = 0.4 M.

questions.q: A 12V battery with internal resistance 1Ω is connected across two parallel resistors of 6Ω and 3Ω. Calculate the current supplied.
questions.exp: Parallel resistance R_p = (6×3)/(6+3) = 2Ω. Total circuit resistance = 2 + 1 = 3Ω. Current I = 12 / 3 = 4.0 A.
